KIKO BATS FOR DAM SAFETY, CREATION OF DISASTER RISK DEPARTMENT

Senator Kiko Pangilinan is calling for urgent action to strengthen the country's disaster preparedness through the passage of two key measures: the Dam Safety Act and the Disaster and Emergency Act of 2025.

Filed amid growing risks from climate change and extreme weather events, the proposed laws aim to protect lives, livelihoods, and critical infrastructure—especially as Metro Manila and nearby provinces reel from days of heavy flooding caused by the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Crising.

"We cannot afford to be reactive when our lives, livelihoods, and infrastructure are at risk," Pangilinan said. "Prevention is better than relief packs, evacuation centers, and ayuda."

Under the Dam Safety Act, a National Dam Safety Authority will be established to oversee the operations and early warning systems of all dams nationwide. It will also implement a comprehensive safety program to minimize socio-economic and environmental risks.

Meanwhile, the Disaster and Emergency Act of 2025 seeks to create a Department of Disaster and Emergency Management, which will replace the current NDRRMC and Office of Civil Defense. The new department will integrate disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation efforts, and lead the coordination of emergency response programs.

Pangilinan urged fellow lawmakers and the national government to adopt a science-based, proactive approach: "It's time to build a safer and more resilient future. We have to shift from a culture of reaction to a culture of preparedness and prevention."

MMDA to Implement Zipper Lane Along Elliptical corner Commonwealth Ave for PBBM’s 4th SONA on July 28

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) will implement a zipper lane or counterflow along Commonwealth Avenue to give way to vehicles of government officials and guests going to the Batasang Pambansa in Quezon City for President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s fourth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 28.

Motorists are advised to take alternate routes to avoid the anticipated heavy traffic along Commonwealth Avenue and IBP Road.

ALTERNATE ROUTES:
NORTHBOUND (Quezon Memorial Circle to Fairview)
• Vehicles from Elliptical Road should take North Avenue, right turn at Mindanao Avenue, then right turn to Sauyo Road, or take Quirino Highway to reach the point of destination.
SOUTHBOUND (Fairview to Quezon Memorial Circle)
• Vehicles from Commonwealth Avenue should take Sauyo Road or Quirino Highway, turn left at Mindanao Avenue, then turn left at North Avenue to reach the point of destination.
FOR LIGHT VEHICLES
• Light vehicles from C5 Road may turn left at Magiting St., turn right at Maginhawa St., turn left at Mayaman St. to Kalayaan Avenue to reach the point of destination.
FOR TRUCKS
• All trucks coming from C-5 along Katipunan Avenue should take the Luzon Flyover then turn left at Congressional Avenue to reach the point of destination.

According to MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes, a total of 1,329 personnel from various units will be deployed to man and manage both vehicular and pedestrian traffic, respond to emergencies, clear roads, and assist in crowd control.

A no-day-off, no-absent policy will be strictly implemented for field traffic personnel.

Ambulances, tow trucks, fire trucks, mobile patrol units, motorcycle units, flood mitigation equipment, and other resources will also be deployed at designated routes and staging areas.

Traffic advisory signage will be put along alternate routes to guide motorists. Plastic barriers and traffic cones will also be installed along zipper lanes and affected roads.

The MMDA Mobile Command Center, equipped with CCTV monitors, will also be stationed at Batasan corner Commonwealth area.

SONA protest actions will be monitored at the MMDA Communications and Command Center located in Pasig City.

The MMDA Special Operations Group-Task Force started conducting road and sidewalk clearing operations in the vicinity of the Batasang Pambansa Complex to ensure that all illegally-parked vehicles and sidewalk vendors were removed so that alternate routes will be fully passable and obstruction-free for motorists.
